mainTopic: Whether שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב count for שמחה (עולא vs. רבין), and רב כהנא's source for when the אימורים of the חגיגה become פסול
overview: This amud opens at the end of עולא's ruling. שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not count for שמחה, because they were not slaughtered at a time of rejoicing. They also do not count for חגיגה, because an obligation must come from חולין. A proof for עולא from a ברייתא about the first and last nights of the festival is rejected, because the ברייתא gives its own reason: only a night with days of rejoicing before it is included. רב יוסף and רבא challenge עולא. The answers are that the חגיגה of the fourteenth was really slaughtered on the fifteenth, and that on a שבת יום טוב one rejoices with clean clothes and old wine. רבין then reports a different version in the name of רבי אלעזר: such שלמים do count for שמחה, and the same ברייתא is no proof against him. Next, רב כהנא learns from the word ״ראשית״ that the אימורים of the חגיגה of the fifteenth must be offered before the first morning. רב יוסף, אביי and רבא debate whether that extra word is really needed. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about meat, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: עולא's reason why the offering does not count for rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: This finishes עולא's first reason. שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not fulfill שמחה, because the slaughter has to happen at a time of rejoicing, and it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The slaughter must be] at a time of rejoicing, and here it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins mid-sentence. We are hearing the end of עולא's explanation of why שלמים slaughtered before the festival do not count for the מצוה of שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא holds that the מצוה of שמחה depends on when the animal was slaughtered, not only on when it is eaten. The day before יום טוב (the fourteenth of the month) is not yet a time of rejoicing. So meat slaughtered then cannot fulfill שמחה, even if it is eaten on the festival itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to rejoice on the festival, done by eating שלמים meat
At the time of rejoicing, meaning on the festival itself
And it is not so / that is missing here

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not when the meat is eaten. It is when the animal was slaughtered. Meat eaten on יום טוב still does not count if the animal was slaughtered on ערב יום טוב.

phrases.english: at the time of rejoicing, and it is not.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence: we need the animal slaughtered at a time of rejoicing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes עולא's statement, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not fulfill שמחה, because the slaughter was not at a time of rejoicing.

steps.title: עולא's reason why the offering does not count for the festival offering
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives his second reason. These שלמים also do not fulfill חגיגה, because חגיגה is an obligation, and an obligatory offering must come from unconsecrated animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for חגיגה: it is an obligation, and anything that is an obligation can only come from unconsecrated property.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains why the same offering cannot count toward the separate obligation of קרבן חגיגה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרבן חגיגה is a required offering. A required offering cannot be paid with an animal that was already sanctified for a different purpose. These שלמים were already consecrated before יום טוב, so they cannot double as the חגיגה.

keyTerms.meaning: Something one is obligated to bring

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב fail on two counts. They fail for שמחה because the slaughter was not at a time of rejoicing. They fail for חגיגה because an obligation must come from חולין.

phrases.english: Regarding the festival offering:
it is something that is an obligation,
and anything that is an obligation
comes only from unconsecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of עולא's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These שלמים do not fulfill חגיגה, because an obligatory offering must come from חולין.

steps.title: A proposed proof from a teaching about the last night of the festival
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports עולא. The ברייתא learns from the words 'וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ' that the last night of the festival is included in שמחה, and the word אַךְ excludes the first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? 'And you shall be but joyous' comes to include the last night of the festival in the מצוה of rejoicing. Do you say it means the last night, or perhaps only the first night? The verse says 'but' (אַךְ), which limits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא it thinks may back up עולא. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains how it would prove עולא's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that the night of the last יום טוב has a מצוה of שמחה, while the first night does not. The limiting word אַךְ is what tells us one of the nights is left out. The proof depends on why the first night is the one left out, and the next step spells out that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say that [a source] supports him?
'And you shall be but joyous' (דברים טז:טו)
Divided/limited; the word אַךְ restricts the rule

phrases.english: Let us say that [a ברייתא] supports him:
'And you shall be but joyous' —

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה.
phrases.english: to include the night of the last festival day in rejoicing.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן,
phrases.english: Do you say the night of the last festival day,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: or is it perhaps only the night of the first festival day?
The verse says: 'but (joyous)' — it limits.
phrases.notes: אַךְ is a limiting word, so one night is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a possible support for עולא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not count for שמחה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding 'וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ' that includes the last night and excludes the first night

steps.title: How the teaching would prove עולא right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the proof. The first night is excluded because a person has nothing valid to rejoice with. Meat slaughtered on ערב יום טוב does not count, just as עולא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason [the first night is excluded]? Is it not because he has nothing with which to rejoice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the logic of the proof. The first night lacks שמחה only because, according to עולא, there is no valid meat available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No offerings are slaughtered at night. So on the first night of יום טוב, the only meat available was slaughtered on ערב יום טוב, and עולא says that meat does not count. On the last night, there is meat from the day before, which was חול המועד, already a time of rejoicing. This would explain the ברייתא's distinction perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not because...? (a rhetorical push toward an answer)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מַאי טַעְמָא' looks like a real question, but here it is part of the proof. The גמרא is pushing toward the answer that supports עולא.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין לוֹ בַּמֶּה יִשְׂמַח!
phrases.english: Is it not because he has nothing with which to rejoice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted ברייתא supports עולא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא excludes the first night, presumably because there is no valid meat for שמחה

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the teaching gives its own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא itself explains that the last night is included because days of rejoicing come before it, and the first night has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is for the reason that was taught: What did you see to include the last night and exclude the first night? I include the last night, because there is rejoicing before it. I exclude the first night, because there is no rejoicing before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The first night is excluded for a different reason, which the ברייתא states openly, so it gives no support to עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reason has nothing to do with when the meat was slaughtered. The last night is attached to the days of rejoicing that came before it. The first night has no rejoicing before it to carry over. So the ברייתא fits even someone who disagrees with עולא, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: As the reason was taught [in the ברייתא itself]
What did you see [to rule this way]?

steps.whatToRemember: The attempted support for עולא fails. The ברייתא excludes the first night only because no festival days of rejoicing come before it. That reason has nothing to do with meat slaughtered on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. A proof fails when the source gives its own reason, and that reason does not depend on the opinion being proven.

phrases.english: No, it is as the reason was taught:

phrases.aramaic: מָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן
phrases.english: What did you see to include the night of the last festival day
and to exclude the night of the first festival day?

phrases.aramaic: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן
phrases.english: I include the night of the last festival day,
since there is rejoicing before it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: and I exclude the night of the first festival day,
since there is no rejoicing before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in steps 3 and 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. עולא's ruling itself is not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the first night is excluded for lack of valid meat. The ברייתא explicitly says it is because no days of rejoicing come before it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא does not support עולא. His ruling stands without proof from this source.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges עולא from the festival offering of the fourteenth
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: the חגיגה of the fourteenth fulfills שמחה. That seems to contradict עולא's rule that the slaughter must be at a time of rejoicing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: A ברייתא says the חגיגה offering of the fourteenth fulfills the מצוה of שמחה, but not the מצוה of חגיגה. Why should it fulfill שמחה? We need the slaughter to happen at a time of rejoicing, and here it did not!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא that seems to go against עולא. It says an animal slaughtered on the fourteenth, before the festival, does count for שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said that שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב do not fulfill שמחה. The ברייתא says the חגיגת ארבעה עשר, which is normally slaughtered on the fourteenth, does fulfill שמחה. The second half of the ברייתא, that it does not count for חגיגה, fits עולא's second reason, but the first half seems to contradict his first reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival שלמים offering brought on the fourteenth of ניסן together with the קרבן פסח
One fulfills an obligation with it
Slaughter at a time of rejoicing, meaning during the festival

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
The festival offering of the fourteenth,
one fulfills with it the מצוה of rejoicing,
but one does not fulfill with it the מצוה of the festival offering.
phrases.notes: This half matches עולא's second reason: an obligation cannot come from an animal that was already consecrated.

phrases.english: Why?
Don't we require slaughter at a time of rejoicing?
And there isn't one here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attempted proof for עולא was rejected, the גמרא now brings a challenge against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that שמחה requires slaughter during the festival
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the חגיגה of the fourteenth fulfills שמחה even though it was slaughtered before the festival.

steps.title: The animal was slaughtered later, on the festival
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין answers that the ברייתא is about a case where the owner delayed and slaughtered the חגיגה on the fifteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: The ברייתא is talking about a case where he delayed and slaughtered it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא. The ברייתא is not about an animal slaughtered on the fourteenth. It is about one that was set aside for the fourteenth but slaughtered on the fifteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is still called 'חגיגת ארבעה עשר' because that was what it was designated for. Since it was actually slaughtered on יום טוב, a time of rejoicing, it fits עולא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He delayed and slaughtered it (on the fifteenth)

steps.confusionAlert: The name 'חגיגת ארבעה עשר' describes what the animal was designated for. It does not describe when it was actually slaughtered.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
It is a case where he delayed and slaughtered it.
phrases.notes: He slaughtered it on the fifteenth, which is יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the ברייתא (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא refers to an animal slaughtered on the fourteenth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to an animal designated for the fourteenth but slaughtered on the fifteenth.

steps.title: רב אשי shows this reading is reasonable, based on בן תימא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports the answer. The ברייתא follows בן תימא, and בן תימא holds that this offering becomes invalid overnight. So it must have been slaughtered on the fifteenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That is also logical. If you don't say so, who taught this ברייתא? בן תימא. But according to בן תימא, leaving it overnight disqualifies it! Learn from this that it was slaughtered on the fifteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives proof that רב אידי בר אבין's reading is correct, based on who wrote the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן תימא holds that the חגיגה of the fourteenth may be eaten only until morning, like the קרבן פסח. If it had been slaughtered on the fourteenth, it could be eaten only on the first night of יום טוב, which is not a time of שמחה (as step 5 showed), and by the day of the fifteenth it would already be invalid. So the ברייתא, which says it fulfills שמחה, must be about an animal slaughtered on the fifteenth.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical, a phrase introducing support for an answer
It becomes invalid by being left overnight

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof secures עולא's position against רב יוסף's challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
So too it is logical,
for if you do not say so,
who teaches this ברייתא?
Ben Teima.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן תֵּימָא הָא פָּסְלָה לַהּ בְּלִינָה!
phrases.english: But Ben Teima disqualifies it by its being left overnight!
phrases.notes: If it had been slaughtered on the fourteenth, it would already be invalid on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Learn from this that it was slaughtered on the fifteenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of רב אידי בר אבין.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the ברייתא refers to an animal slaughtered on the fifteenth
steps.raayaSupportSource: בן תימא's view that the חגיגת ארבעה עשר becomes invalid by לינה

steps.title: רבא challenges עולא from eight days of rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה (in סוכה) that שמחה lasts eight days on סוכות. Under עולא's rule, when the first day falls on שבת, there would be only seven days of שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: A משנה says הלל and שמחה are for eight days. If you say the slaughter must be at a time of rejoicing, there are many times you will find only seven days, such as when the first day of יום טוב falls on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new challenge against עולא from the rule that שמחה lasts all eight days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, private שלמים may not be slaughtered. Meat slaughtered on Friday does not count, according to עולא. So when the first day of סוכות is on שבת, there would be no way to fulfill שמחה that day, and the משנה's eight days would become seven.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל and rejoicing are for eight days (on סוכות)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
הלל and rejoicing are for eight days.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בָּעֵינַן זְבִיחָה בִּשְׁעַת שִׂמְחָה,
phrases.english: And if you say we require slaughter at a time of rejoicing,
then there are many times
when you find only seven,
such as when the first day of the festival falls
on שבת!
phrases.notes: Private שלמים are not slaughtered on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, new challenge against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that the slaughter for שמחה must happen during the festival
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first day of סוכות is on שבת, no valid שמחה meat is possible that day, yet the משנה says שמחה lasts eight days.

steps.title: One rejoices with the festival goats
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהודה answers that on such a שבת, one rejoices with the שעירי הרגלים, which are communal offerings and may be slaughtered on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהודה, said: He rejoices with the goats of the festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an answer for עולא. There is still meat slaughtered on that שבת that can be used for שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעירי הרגלים are communal חטאות brought on each festival. Communal offerings override שבת, so they are slaughtered that same day, and their meat could provide שמחה.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes him rejoice / he rejoices
The goats brought as communal sin-offerings on the festivals

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehuda said:
He rejoices with the goats of the festivals.
phrases.notes: Communal offerings may be slaughtered on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying an alternative source of valid שמחה meat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No meat is slaughtered on שבת, so there is no שמחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The festival goats are slaughtered on שבת and can serve for שמחה.

steps.title: רבא gives two reasons the goats do not work
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the answer. On שבת the goats can only be eaten raw, and raw meat is no rejoicing. Also, only כהנים eat them, so ordinary ישראלים would have nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two refutations. First, the festival goats are eaten raw but not roasted, and there is no rejoicing with raw meat. Also, the כהנים eat them, so with what do the ישראלים rejoice?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב הונא's answer with two separate arguments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting the meat is not part of the service itself, so it may not be done on שבת. That leaves only raw meat, which gives no real joy. Even setting that aside, a חטאת is eaten only by כהנים, so it cannot be the שמחה for the whole nation.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this matter

phrases.english: Rava said: There are two refutations of this:
One, that the festival goats
are eaten raw; they are not eaten roasted,
phrases.notes: Roasting is forbidden on שבת because it is not part of the service.

phrases.english: and there is no rejoicing with raw meat.
And furthermore, the כהנים eat them,
so with what do ordinary ישראלים rejoice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects using the festival goats for שמחה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The goats can only be eaten raw on שבת, and only כהנים eat them.

steps.title: Rejoicing with clean clothes and old wine
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives the final answer. On such a day, one rejoices with clean clothes and old wine, so there are still eight days of שמחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: He rejoices with clean clothing and old wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new answer that saves עולא's rule and also keeps eight days of שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of שמחה is not limited to eating שלמים. When no valid שלמים are possible, a person fulfills שמחה through other things that bring joy, like clean clothes and aged wine. So the eight days stay intact, and עולא's rule about slaughter still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals a replacement for the rejected answer

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's rule survives both challenges. The חגיגה of the fourteenth counts for שמחה only when it was slaughtered on the fifteenth. When the first day of סוכות falls on שבת, שמחה is fulfilled with clean clothes and old wine.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
He rejoices with clean clothing and old wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening how שמחה can be fulfilled
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמחה can only be fulfilled with sacrificial meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: When no שלמים are possible, שמחה is fulfilled with clean clothes and old wine.

steps.title: רבין's version: offerings slaughtered before the festival count for rejoicing but not for the festival offering
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי אלעזר said שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב count for שמחה but not for חגיגה, and the גמרא explains why.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: if someone slaughtered שלמים on ערב יום טוב, they count for the מצוה of שמחה, but not for the מצוה of חגיגה. They count for שמחה because the slaughtering does not have to happen during the time of rejoicing. They do not count for חגיגה because חגיגה is an obligation, and anything that is an obligation may only come from חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין brings a new version of רבי אלעזר's view, and it disagrees with עולא's rule. The גמרא then explains both halves of the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא held that שלמים slaughtered before יום טוב do not count for שמחה. רבין says they do, because only the eating has to be during יום טוב, not the slaughtering. They still fail for חגיגה for a different reason. An animal already set aside as שלמים is not חולין, and an obligation cannot be paid with something that is already הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The מצוה to rejoice on יום טוב by eating שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves fail or succeed for different reasons. The problem with חגיגה is not the timing of the slaughter. The problem is that obligations must come from חולין.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
peace-offerings that one slaughtered on the eve of the Festival
one fulfills with them the מצוה of rejoicing
but one does not fulfill with them the Festival offering.
One fulfills rejoicing —
because we do not require slaughter at the time of rejoicing.
But not the Festival offering —
because it is something obligatory,
and anything obligatory
comes only from unconsecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a competing version of רבי אלעזר that rejects עולא's rule that such שלמים do not count for שמחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלמים slaughtered on ערב יום טוב count for שמחה, since slaughter need not be at the time of rejoicing. They do not count for חגיגה, since obligations come only from חולין.

steps.title: A ברייתא excludes the first night of the festival from rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from the word ״אך״ that the last night of יום טוב is included in שמחה, but the first night is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged רבין: the פסוק says ״וְהָיִיתָ אַךְ שָׂמֵחַ״. This comes to include the night of the last יום טוב in שמחה. Do you say it includes the last night, or maybe it includes the first night? The פסוק says ״אך״, which limits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a challenge against רבין by quoting a ברייתא. The actual argument against him comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the night of the first יום טוב has no מצוה of שמחה. By itself this does not yet attack רבין. The גמרא will next suggest a reason for the ruling that conflicts with his view.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And you shall be but joyous" —

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן לְשִׂמְחָה.
phrases.english: to include the night of the last Festival day in rejoicing.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן,
phrases.english: Do you say it comes to include the night of the last Festival day,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: or perhaps it is only to include the night of the first Festival day?
The verse states "but" — it restricts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the source used to challenge רבין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's version of רבי אלעזר, that שלמים slaughtered before יום טוב count for שמחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא excludes the first night from שמחה, which hints that nothing valid is available to rejoice with that night.

steps.title: The suggested reason: there is nothing to rejoice with on the first night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא excludes the first night because a person has no valid meat to rejoice with, which contradicts רבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the first night is left out? Is it not because the person has nothing to rejoice with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge against רבין. It suggests the reason for the ברייתא, and that reason contradicts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first night, the only available שלמים were slaughtered on ערב יום טוב. If the reason there is no שמחה is that he has nothing to rejoice with, then those שלמים must not count. That matches עולא and goes against רבין.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not? (introduces a suggested reason)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין לוֹ בַּמֶּה יִשְׂמַח!
phrases.english: Is it not because he has nothing with which to rejoice!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא that turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's ruling that ערב יום טוב שלמים count for שמחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ערב יום טוב שלמים counted, there would be something to rejoice with on the first night. Excluding that night shows they do not count.

steps.title: A different reason: the first night has no rejoicing before it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The ברייתא itself explains that the last night is included because days of rejoicing come before it, while the first night has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. As the ברייתא teaches: why include the last night and leave out the first night? I include the last night because there was rejoicing before it. I leave out the first night because there was no rejoicing before it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבין by showing that the ברייתא has a different reason for its ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exclusion of the first night has nothing to do with whether the meat is valid. It comes from a rule about nights: a night joins the שמחה only when days of שמחה came before it. So the ברייתא is no proof against רבין, and his view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
What did you see? (Why choose this side?)

steps.whatToRemember: The first night of יום טוב is not part of the מצוה of שמחה because no days of שמחה come before it. The reason is not a lack of valid meat, so רבין's view survives.

phrases.english: No, it is as it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: מָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן
phrases.english: What did you see to include the night of the last Festival day
and to exclude the night of the first Festival day?

phrases.aramaic: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן
phrases.english: I include the night of the last Festival day
for there is rejoicing before it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹצִיא אֲנִי לֵילֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: and I exclude the night of the first Festival day
for there is no rejoicing before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 15 and so removes the challenge to רבין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers an alternative reason for the ruling, taken from the ברייתא itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first night is excluded because ערב יום טוב שלמים are not valid for שמחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first night is excluded because no days of שמחה precede it. This says nothing about whether ערב יום טוב שלמים are valid.

steps.title: Source that the altar parts of the fifteenth's festival offering are disqualified overnight
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns from the closeness of ״ולא ילין חלב חגי עד בקר״ to the word ״ראשית״ that the אימורים of the חגיגה of the fifteenth become פסול after the first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: where do we learn that the אימורים of the חגיגה of the fifteenth become פסול if left overnight? The פסוק says: ״וְלֹא יָלִין חֵלֶב חַגִּי עַד בֹּקֶר״. Right next to it comes the word ״רֵאשִׁית״. This teaches that the morning mentioned here is the first morning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא starts a new topic. He brings a פסוק as the source for a rule about the altar parts of the חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of the חגיגה of the fifteenth may be eaten for two days, so one might think the אימורים may also wait. רב כהנא uses the word right next to the פסוק (סמיכות) to teach that ״בקר״ means the first morning. So the אימורים must be offered before the first morning, even though the meat itself lasts longer.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an offering burned on the מזבח
Being left overnight, which makes an offering פסול
Placed right next to it (a learning from closeness)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that even though the meat of the חגיגה of the fifteenth lasts two days, its אימורים must be offered before the first morning. The rest of the amud debates whether the word ״ראשית״ is really needed for this.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
From where do we know that the sacrificial parts of the Festival offering of the fifteenth
are disqualified by being left overnight?
As it is stated:
"Neither shall the fat of My Festival offering remain until morning,"
and right next to it is "first"
to say that this morning —
is the first morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the scriptural source for when the אימורים of the חגיגה of the fifteenth become פסול through לינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אימורים of the חגיגה of the fifteenth become פסול if left past the first morning. This is learned from the closeness of ״ראשית״ to ״עד בקר״.

steps.title: רב יוסף questions why the word 'first' is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects to רב כהנא. Without ״ראשית״ we would read ״בקר״ as the second morning, which would create an impossible case: the meat is פסול by evening while the אימורים last until morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: According to you, the reason we know it is the first morning is that the Torah wrote ״ראשית״. So if it had not written ״ראשית״, I would have said that ״בקר״ means the second morning. But is there any case where the meat becomes פסול in the evening, while the אימורים stay valid until the morning?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב כהנא's proof from step 17. He argues that the word ״ראשית״ is not needed, because the other reading makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a חגיגה may be eaten for two days and the night between them, so it becomes פסול when the second night begins. If ״בקר״ meant the second morning, the אימורים would still be valid at a time when the meat is already פסול. רב יוסף assumes that such a case does not exist, so ״ראשית״ should be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'First'; the word רב כהנא used for his proof
The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying that רב כהנא's הלכה is wrong. He agrees that the אימורים become פסול after the first night. He is only asking why the word ״ראשית״ is needed to teach it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
The reason is that it wrote 'first',
but had it not written 'first',
I would have said: what is 'morning'?
The second morning.
phrases.notes: Meaning the morning of the seventeenth.

phrases.english: Is there anything where the meat
becomes disqualified from the evening,
while the sacrificial parts are valid until morning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's derivation from step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's need for the word ״ראשית״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The other reading would give the impossible result that the meat becomes פסול before the אימורים do. So the extra word should not be needed.

steps.title: אביי shows such a case exists: the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the case does exist. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the meat of the פסח becomes פסול at midnight, but its אימורים are valid until morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why not? Look at the פסח according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Its meat becomes פסול at midnight, yet its אימורים may be offered until morning!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רב כהנא. He shows that a case where the meat becomes פסול before the אימורים really does exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's question rested on the idea that the meat can never become פסול earlier than the אימורים. אביי shows a clear example of exactly that, which is the פסח according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. So the 'second morning' reading is possible, and ״ראשית״ is needed after all.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Why not?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי פֶּסַח לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: For there is the Paschal offering according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
whose meat is disqualified from midnight,
while the sacrificial parts are valid until morning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question by giving a real example
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counterexample that knocks down the assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A case where the meat becomes פסול before the אימורים cannot exist, so ״ראשית״ is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a case exists (the פסח according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה), so ״ראשית״ is needed.

steps.title: רבא restates what truly bothered רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב יוסף's real question is different. A תנא reads ״בקר״ by meat without needing ״ראשית״, so why should רב כהנא need ״ראשית״ for the אימורים, which are holier?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is what really bothered רב יוסף. Is there any case where the תנא does not need ״ראשית״ for the meat, but רב כהנא needs ״ראשית״ for the אימורים?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new, sharper version of רב יוסף's question, which avoids אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer whether such a case can exist. The question is now about how the verses are read. A תנא understands ״בקר״ by meat as the first morning with no extra word. The אימורים are holier and become פסול more easily than meat, so they should certainly not need an extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was difficult for him
A Sage of the משנה period, here the author of a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with אביי's example. He is saying that אביי misunderstood what רב יוסף was asking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the debate from 'is such a הלכה possible?' to 'how do we read the verses?'. That is why the גמרא now needs to find the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what was difficult to Rav Yosef:
Is there anything like this, that the tanna
does not need 'first' for the meat,
while Rav Kahana needs 'first' for the sacrificial parts?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רב יוסף's challenge from step 18 so that אביי's answer in step 19 no longer works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If meat, which is less holy, needs no extra word to mean the first morning, then אימורים, which are holier, certainly should not need one.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source רבא mentioned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of the תנא רבא was referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching of the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask where we see that the תנא reads ״בקר״ by meat without ״ראשית״. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's question in step 20 depends on a source he did not quote. Before the challenge can stand, the גמרא must identify that source.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רבא's question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ברייתא in which a תנא reads ״בקר״ by meat without needing ״ראשית״

steps.title: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא on the meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by starting to quote a ברייתא on the פסוק ״לא ילין מן הבשר אשר תזבח בערב ביום הראשון לבקר״. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: ״Nor shall any of the meat that you sacrifice on the first day at evening remain overnight until the morning.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא that רבא was referring to. This is a setup line, and the ברייתא's explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק speaks about meat and uses the word ״בקר״. Here the תנא will explain ״בקר״ without relying on the word ״ראשית״. That is the basis of רבא's challenge to רב כהנא.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
'Nor shall any of the meat remain overnight
that you sacrifice at evening
on the first day until the morning'
phrases.notes: This verse is from דברים טז:ד. The ברייתא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 21 by quoting the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא on דברים טז:ד. The quote continues on the next amud.
